title: QBR-ready customer health model & renewal playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic, QBR-friendly customer health scoring model and an associated renewal playbook. Goal: give CSMs an action-oriented single-sheet that (1) surfaces risk early, (2) prioritizes outreach for renewals, and (3) feeds a weekly renewal tracker.

Context / scope:
- Focus is on mid-market and enterprise accounts using Redwood Hosted + Dedicated.
- Includes signals across usage, reliability, product adoption, and relationship health.
- Designed for QBR prep (one-pager summary) and for the weekly renewal pipeline review.

High-level approach (do not over-fit):
1) Score = weighted sum of independent signal buckets (Usage, Reliability, Product Adoption, Financial/Contract, Relationship).
2) Normalize each bucket to 0-100, apply weights, then map final score to risk band: Healthy (80-100), Watch (60-79), At-Risk (40-59), Critical (<40).
3) Flag-based overrides: any Critical reliability incident in last 30 days = max(At-Risk unless CEO-level escalation present).

Signal buckets and suggested metrics (examples):
- Usage (weight 30):
  * Weekly active routes (relative to onboarding baseline) — threshold: >90% baseline -> 100, 50-90% -> 50-80, <50% -> 20
  * Token throughput trend (7d) — sustained drop >30% vs prior quarter -> negative points
  * Feature breadth: number of distinct API endpoints in production (chat, embeddings, rerank) normalized to customer cohort

- Reliability & Performance (weight 25):
  * Error rate (5xx, timeouts) 30d average — 0% -> 100, >2% -> degrade linearly
  * Average response latency vs SLA — >2x SLA penalized heavily
  * Incidents: number of Sev1/Sev2 in 90d with customer impact (list dates and summary)

- Product Adoption (weight 20):
  * Feature usage: embeddings adoption (yes/no) as binary boost
  * Console adoption: daily active users in their org using Redwood Console -> encourages self-serve
  * Rollout depth: percent traffic on Redwood vs fallback model after rollouts

- Financial / Contract (weight 15):
  * Billing issues (open invoices, disputes) -> binary flag reduces score
  * Seat expansion requests or committed capacity changes (positive)
  * Contract end date proximity: <90 days -> increases urgency score weight in pipeline view

- Relationship / Org Health (weight 10):
  * Executive sponsor contact frequency (last 90 days) -> recency score
  * CSM meeting cadence adherence (>=monthly)
  * NPS / qualitative sentiment from support tickets or CSM notes (manual tag)

Risk flags (immediate attention):
- Flag: Drop-in-production-traffic (>30% drop week-over-week) -> requires automated alert to CS leads and SRE/eng triage
- Flag: New billing dispute opened -> Sales ops + CSM ownership until resolved
- Flag: 2+ Sev incidents with customer impact in last 60 days -> Elevate to escalation playbook
- Flag: CSM not able to reach PO/exec after 3 attempts in 30 days -> qualify as engagement risk

Sample scoring worksheet (to paste into a QBR slide/table):
Columns: metric | raw value | normalized (0-100) | weight | weighted score | notes
Example row: Weekly active routes | 420 (baseline 600) | 70 | 30% -> 21 points | note: rollout paused in staging

Mapping to action for QBR / renewal:
- Healthy (80+) -> standard QBR + upsell opportunities slide; sales notify for expansion plays
- Watch (60-79) -> CSM cadence increased to biweekly; prepare feature adoption play (see playbook section)
- At-Risk (40-59) -> renewal manager + solutions engineer join QBR; propose technical review and cost/latency tuning; consider short-term credits if outage-related
- Critical (<40) -> exec escalation; consider remediation SOW and pause automated renewal until corrective plan in place

Renewal playbook (quick checklist for deals <180 days out):
1) 180d+: Start renewal worksheet, confirm contract terms, map exec sponsor
2) 120d: Health score required; if Watch or worse, open 'pre-renewal remediation' Jira (suggest label: pre-renew-<account>) and schedule technical deep-dive
3) 60d: Present renewal terms and remediation commitments; if At-Risk/Critical, loop in sales director
4) 30d: Finalize paperwork or escalate to GTM director for retention incentives
5) Post-renewal: capture lessons in Confluence page and update scoring weights if needed

Suggested play snippets by risk type:
- Low adoption play: Goal = surface quick wins in 30 days
  * Send adoption checklist (3 low-effort integrations)
  * 2-week implementation assist session with solutions engineer
  * Run a traffic pilot on a secondary route with warm cache to show perf improvement
- Reliability play: Goal = stabilize and rebuild trust
  * Triage + RCA within 72 hours; share action plan with customer
  * Offer a monitoring dashboard view and weekly sync until SLA met
  * Consider temporary capacity bump (Dedicated burst) for mission-critical peaks
- Financial friction play: Goal = clear billing to remove blocker
  * Introduce Finance ops contact; create shared ticket with PO and invoices attached
  * Propose staggered payment options or short-term credits for outage-related losses (with legal sign-off)

QBR one-pager template (to drop into slide):
- Account overview: ARR, contract term, product mix
- Health score (big number) + risk band color
- Top 3 signals driving score (bullets)
- Last 90d incidents and status
- Adoption wins / blockers
- Renewal timeline and recommended next steps

Operational notes / TODOs (internal):
- [ ] Build a weekly ETL that produces normalized signals into the CS dashboard (owners: eng-metrics + cs-ops). Jira: CS-842
- [ ] Create a lightweight scoring UI in the Console for CSM overrides (scope: read/write notes, add flags). Owner: console-and-tooling
- [ ] Run a dry-run on 5 pilot accounts (AMX, Beta-tier customers) in Jan to validate thresholds. Owner: customer-success, due 2026-01-15
- [ ] Draft email template for Watch -> At-Risk outreach; include playbook links and SRE contact

Unresolved questions / discussion points:
- Should we surface model-predicted churn probability (ML) or keep rules-based for transparency to CSMs? Pros/cons noted in comments below.
- Are weights different for Dedicated-only customers (likely reliability weight should increase)? Proposal: +10% reliability weight for Dedicated accounts, reduce usage by 5%.

Notes / context links referenced in conversation:
- Existing renewal tracker (internal sheet): sheets/redwood/cs-renewal-pipeline (see linked_artifacts)
- Background on console adoption metrics: confluence:product/console-adoption-metrics

Author notes (Asha):
This is intentionally prescriptive to make it easy for CSMs to operationalize before we build more product automation. Keep feedback coming — ping me in #cs-playbooks or add comments to the Confluence draft.

Revision history summary:
- 2025-11-02 initial draft with buckets and weights
- 2025-11-12 added reliability play and risk flags after ops sync
- 2025-11-20 updated renewal checklist and added pilot next-steps
